item.title: US set for largest mass visa revocation in history targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, officials say
item.description: The Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States.

item.title: Thousands are still without power in Gary, Ind., nearly two weeks after storms
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Kaitlin Washburn, reporter with the Chicago Sun-Times, about the ongoing power outages in northwest Indiana and how they're affecting residents' lives.

item.title: Will the newest plan to remove tariffs on beef imports help or hurt U.S. ranchers
item.description: Oren Lesmeister, a fifth-generation cattle rancher in South Dakota, reacts to the announcement of 300,000 metric tons of beef being imported to the US in an attempt to lower beef prices.

item.title: Supreme Court gives Trump an interim win on his mail voting order, but hurdles loom
item.description: The Supreme Court paused a lower court's ruling that blocked key parts of Trump's order to limit voting by mail for the midterms. But U.S. Postal Service work on the order remains blocked nationwide.

item.title: Sean Grayson, former deputy convicted of killing Sonya Massey, dies in prison, lawyer says
item.description: Sean Grayson, a former Illinois sheriff's deputy whose fatal shooting of Sonya Massey inside her home became a flashpoint over police use of force, died Sunday while serving a 20-year prison sentence.

item.title: Navy holds town hall to reassure military families displaced by Iran war
item.description: Hundreds of military families were evacuated from Bahrain during the opening days of the war with Iran. The Navy recently held a town hall to try to reassure them that they had not been forgotten.

item.title: Thousands of Indiana residents without power 2 weeks after powerful storm
item.description: Two weeks after extreme weather in Northwest Indiana, more than 10,000 are still without power. Some residents worry that Gary, a predominantly Black city, may be the last to see the lights go on.
